title: OMB President's Budget data (Historical Tables, Public Budget Database, Federal Credit Supplement) via GovInfo
agency: Office of Management and Budget (published by the U.S. Government Publishing Office, GovInfo)
keywords: budget of the united states government
federal debt held by the public
grants to state and local governments
questions: total federal outlays, receipts and the deficit since 1940 in dollars and as a percent of GDP
federal outlays by budget function or by agency over time
budget authority or outlays for one budget account from the Public Budget Database
credit subsidy rates of federal direct loan and loan guarantee programs
federal debt held by the public as a percent of GDP history

manual.how: Open each link in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser (GovInfo files, no sign-in) and save the file under the name shown, then upload it. If a Historical Tables link opens GovInfo's error page, download the edition's package zip (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BUDGET-<FY>-TAB.zip) and upload that instead. The same files are on whitehouse.gov: Historical Tables at https://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/information-resources/budget/historical-tables/ (hist01z1_fy2027.xlsx ...), the Public Budget Database and Federal Credit Supplement at https://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/information-resources/budget/supplemental-materials/ (outlays_fy2027.xlsx, budauth_fy2027.xlsx, receipts_fy2027.xlsx, cr_supp_fy2027.xlsx); whitehouse.gov keeps only recent editions.

cache.why: Each edition is fixed once published, but files are a few MB at most; data/ is reused within a run.

redistribution.why: The Budget of the U.S. Government is a U.S. government work (17 U.S.C. 105), in the public domain; GovInfo content is free to reuse.

citation: Office of Management and Budget, Budget of the U.S. Government, {dataset}, GovInfo (www.govinfo.gov), retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Which budget edition (fy)? Each edition revises history and adds the President's estimates; the default is the newest edition on GovInfo (FY2027 as of October 2026), and a comparison across years should come from one edition.
Actual years only, or also the budget's estimates (the current year and the President's proposals for the budget year and beyond)? Default: actuals only, with estimates labelled if used.
Nominal dollars, constant (FY 2017) dollars, or percent of GDP? Default: nominal, with percent of GDP from Tables 1.2, 2.3, 3.1 or 7.1 when shares are asked.
